text:
Mike H: Ran a set of KV cache warmup comparisons — replay harness vs synthetic generator. results are weird, asking for sanity check. :eyes:

benchbot: summary report uploaded -> https://internal.redwood/bench/1773123456 (run id 2026-03-18-kv-warmup) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Mike H: TL;DR numbers — replay: hit_rate=0.92, p50=18ms, p95=45ms. synthetic: hit_rate=0.74, p50=22ms, p95=90ms. throughput similar.

Sasha R: ok weird. do we use the same model shard mapping and same seed? synthetic often lacks temporal locality.

Mike H: shard mapping and model binary identical. seed set for request ordering, but synthetic generator samples sequences uniformly from corpus. replay is straight from production traces (sanitized).

Lee W: that explains a lot. replay preserves session stickiness => much higher prefix reuse. synthetic breaks sessions, so warmup is worse. we should control for "session affinity" when comparing.

Jamie K: also saw a correctness blip when running concurrency sweeps on synthetic: about 0.2% of requests returned stale kv entries (different token ids after eviction). not sure if it's harness or runtime bug. :bug:

Mike H: repro steps I used (short):
```
# run synthetic generator at qps 1200, 16 threads
./tools/synth_load --corpus tokens.ndjson --qps 1200 --threads 16 --sessionize 0
# run replay harness
./tools/replay_load --trace prod-sample.trace --qps 1200
```

Jamie K: logs attached in bench report show "kv_lookup: key=X - found but seq!=expected" repeated. looks like an eviction+write race under high concurrency.

Sasha R: can you paste a snippet of the log error?

Jamie K: sure — excerpt: 
```
2026-03-18T10:12:07.123Z [worker-12] kv.get key=conv:12345 seq=9876 -> returned seq=9521
2026-03-18T10:12:07.124Z [evict-thread] evict shard=5 key=conv:12345 freed
2026-03-18T10:12:07.125Z [worker-7] kv.put key=conv:12345 seq=9876 stored
```
Not a deterministic crash, but mismatch visible.

Lee W: sounds like double-checked eviction without proper ordering. we have a window: worker reads pointer, then eviction frees memory, then another worker re-allocates same pointer for new key -> old pointer content observed.

Sasha R: is the runtime using per-shard mutexes or atomic swap for table entries?

Mike H: current impl: per-shard lock for table metadata but we use lock-free epoch reclamation for entries to avoid pause. might be a gap in the reclamation ordering.

Jamie K: quick patch I tried locally: bump epoch check and delay re-use by one GC cycle. no functional regressions and stale reads dropped to 0 in my micro runs, but p95 up ~6ms.

Sasha R: tradeoff expected. we need an apples-to-apples perf comparison though: both harnesses must use identical session stickiness and temporal locality, otherwise we measure different workload.

Mike H: agreed. suggestion: add a synthetic mode that replays session IDs (preserve request ordering per session) and a second axis that scrambles inter-session arrival times. then compare three curves: replay, sessionized-synthetic, fully-random-synthetic.

benchbot: new task created -> PERF-1423: synthetic sessionized generator + reproduce eviction race. assignee: Jamie K.

Lee W: for eviction correctness path we should instrument per-key lifecycle events: alloc, alive-epoch, evicted, reclaimed. minimal tracing only for failure cases. can add a config flag to enable in perf runs.

Mike H: agreed. add a CLI flag to runtime: --kv-trace=failures|all|off. put tracing samples into bench artifacts.

Jamie K: after the fix I re-ran sessionized-synthetic at qps 1k with 32 concurrency: hit_rate=0.88, p50=20ms, p95=51ms. still below replay but much closer. no correctness failures in 2h run.

Sasha R: nice. can we try the GC-delay approach vs per-key reference count? reference counting might avoid p95 hit but add memory overhead.

Mike H: assign two experiments: (A) GC-delay (Jamie) (B) per-key refcount (Lee). measure hit_rate, p50, p95, extra mem, and correctness under concurrency. same sessionized-synthetic workload.

benchbot: experiment jobs started: PERF-1423-A (Jamie), PERF-1423-B (Lee). logs at https://internal.redwood/bench/1773123456/jobs

Sasha R: one more note on apples-to-apples: ensure kernel selection and batching heuristics are identical across runs. kernel variants can change how sequence lengths amortize and affect cache warmup. pin to kernel v3 for these benches.

Mike H: pinned. config below:
```
{ "kernel_version": "3.1.0-pin", "batching": { "max_batch": 64, "batch_timeout_ms": 12 }, "kv": { "shards": 64, "eviction_policy": "lru" }
}
```

Jamie K: quick perf update (first run results):
- replay: hit=0.92 p50=18ms p95=45ms correctness=OK
- session-synth (no fix): hit=0.79 p50=21ms p95=81ms correctness=fail 0.2%
- session-synth (GC-delay): hit=0.88 p50=20ms p95=51ms correctness=OK

Lee W: nice. I'll start refcount patch next; estimate 2d.

Sasha R: can we capture warmup curve (hit rate over time) for all runs and include AUC? that will quantify how fast cache reaches steady state.

Mike H: yes. bench artifacts already include time-series. I'll compute AUC and attach to ticket.

Jamie K: final ask: make sure replay harness doesn't include rare-admin calls that artificially bump locality. filter traces for user traffic only.

Mike H: noted, already filtered but will double-check.

Sasha R: ok plan sounds solid. thanks team. follow-ups on PERF-1423. :thumbsup:
